standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the graded isomorphism to an isomorphism of Proj with matching twists.

core_obligations: Write projective n-space as Proj of the polynomial ring and identify the section s cutting out H with a homogeneous linear form sum a_i T_i (proof lines 6466-6471).

Use the description of the zero scheme of a section to see that on each standard affine D_+(T_j) the ideal of H is generated by sum a_i T_i/T_j, hence that the homogeneous ideal I is generated by sum a_i T_i (proof lines 6472-6482).
Exhibit k[T_0,...,T_n]/I as a polynomial ring in n variables as graded rings, e.g. by sending S_i to the class of T_i when a_n is nonzero (proof lines 6483-6487).
Conclude the isomorphism of Proj by functoriality and identify the twists using the result on surjective graded ring maps generated in degree one (proof lines 6488-6492).
proof_roadmap: Translate the section into a linear form.
Compute the homogeneous ideal of the hyperplane on standard affines.
Identify the quotient graded ring and apply functoriality of Proj.
difficulty_reason: The lemma exhibits an isomorphism from projective (n-1)-space onto any hyperplane H in projective n-space carrying O(1) to the restriction of O(1). The proof writes projective n-space as Proj of a polynomial ring, identifies the section defining H with a linear form, uses the description of the zero scheme to see that the homogeneous ideal of H is generated by that form, exhibits the quotient as a polynomial ring in n variables as graded rings, and obtains the isomorphism by functoriality of Proj; the equality of twists is then read off from the corresponding result on surjective graded ring maps generated in degree one (proof lines 6466-6492). H2: the identification of the homogeneous ideal and the graded-ring isomorphism are the substance and are carried out in detail.
